Asobi 1.0 (build 1051) Sep 30, 2026

  • A truer connection measurement. Review ▸ Network ▸ Measure Now read far too low on fast lines (11 Mbps on a gigabit connection): it timed one small download including the connection setup. It now warms the connection, times only the data arriving, and fills a fast line with four downloads at once. The number is the speed to the review server, which is what fetching media gets; a speed test to a nearby server can read higher.
Earlier updates

1.0 (build 1050) Sep 30, 2026

  • Each tool keeps its colour. Circle in red, switch to Text and type in white, go back to the circle and it is red again. A colour picked with no tool in hand goes to the next tool you pick.
  • T is Text. As in every paint program and on the web page. Trim handles moved to ⇧T.
  • A tick to place text. The text box has a ✓ beside its size buttons; Enter still works.
  • Line opacity that works. It now changes a selected mark, and picking a colour keeps it instead of resetting to solid. Line width, line opacity and fill opacity open as small pop-ups from the palette, and any line width is one pop-up away after the presets. The web toolbar has line opacity too.
  • Who read the brief. The Review Manager shows how many have read the current brief, and who.

1.0 (build 1048) Sep 30, 2026

  • The brief stays with its review. A review brief no longer carries over to other clips or to the next launch; it belongs to the review it was written for. The card only opens over a review.

1.0 (build 1047) Sep 30, 2026

  • Known issues in the brief. The seal on a note marks it Known: it gets a yellow KNOWN tag, it is listed under the brief shot by shot, and anyone typing a note near it is told. The host and studio seats can mark notes.
  • Already noted here. While you type a note, a line above the field shows what has already been said at that moment, so it can be added to instead of repeated. It never stops you sending.
  • Who has read the brief. The host’s card shows who has closed it.

1.0 (build 1045) Sep 30, 2026

  • The review brief. Review ▸ Review Brief… writes a short note that every reviewer sees as a card over the picture, Before we start, the first time they open the review, in the app and on the web. Say what is already known and what to look at, so the notes that come back are about what is new. Change it and everyone sees it once more. The yellow BRIEF tag reopens it. The host and studio seats can write it.
  • Tidier Film Lab. The negative and print menus now run the full width of the panel.

1.0 (build 1042) Sep 30, 2026

  • Halation in the Film Lab. Tick Halation for the red glow film gets around bright lights, from light that bounced off the back of the film and exposed the red layer again. Set its strength, size (in microns on the negative, so it holds from a proxy to the original), threshold, hue from red to orange, a second bounce and a soft scatter. It is added to the scene light before the look, as on film, and shows in the viewer, compare, scopes, grabs and exported movies. It saves with the look and travels with the grade.
  • An eyedropper in the tool palette. The color pop-up has an eyedropper: pick a mark color from anywhere on screen, the picture included.

1.0 (build 1039) Sep 30, 2026

  • One color button in the tool palette. In the column as well as the bar, the palette shows the current color as a single button. Click it and the swatches and the custom color open beside it; picking one closes them. The column is shorter for it.

1.0 (build 1037) Sep 30, 2026

  • Words under the buttons. The control bar now names each button (Play, Loop, Notes and the rest), as the web page does. Turn them off with View ▸ Button Labels (⌥⇧⌘B).
  • A horizontal tool palette. The paint tools can sit as a bar along the top instead of a column. The colors then open from a single color button, as on the web. Switch with the button beside the palette’s grip, or View ▸ Tool Palette Horizontal. Each layout remembers where you put it.
  • The palette comes back when you ask. View ▸ Tool Palette now has a shortcut (⇧⌘P) that works wherever you are. The eye menu’s Tool Palette also brings back a palette hidden with P; before, it could show a tick with no palette.
